claim: For the open XX one-particle operator T_N=4J I-2J A(P_N) with an endpoint potential v_N=-2J+2Ja/L, the scaled quadratic forms converge to 2J(-d^2/dx^2) on [0,1] with phi'(0)=a phi(0), phi(1)=0. The boundary secular equation is sin(qL)+(v_N/(2J))sin(q(L-1))=0; fixed v0 != -2J gives generic Dirichlet low modes. A fixed v0<-2J has a microscopic below-band mode.
quantifiers: For fixed J>0, a in R, and L=N+1 tending to infinity; exact lattice identities hold for every N. The fixed-v0 bound-mode statement applies to v0<-2J.
proof_evidence: Ghost-site boundary recurrence; expansion at q=x/L; discrete-form convergence; exact rational checks for N=1,2 at v=-2J; exact half-line solution v=-4J, r=1/2, E=-J.
costs: O(N) recurrence/form work; no oracle or numerical approximation. Decoder/physical preparation cost not included.
strongest_baseline: Clean sine spectrum and the exact N-particle number-sector archive from cycle 1.
falsifier: A direct substitution into the finite matrix contradicting the displayed secular equation, or a form-limit counterexample under the stated scaling.
prior_art: Kunstatter and Louko, arXiv:1201.2886 (2012), https://arxiv.org/abs/1201.2886; generic Dirichlet and tuned Robin are antecedent context in a different half-line discretization.

claim: A bulk site j_N/L->theta with physical strength 2Jg/L converges to 2J(-d^2+g delta_theta), with continuity and derivative jump phi'(theta+)-phi'(theta-)=g phi(theta). The L^-2 single-site scale vanishes. A distributed potential W(i/L)/L^2 converges to the bounded continuum potential W(x).
quantifiers: Fixed theta in (0,1), finite g, continuous bounded W, J>0; L tends to infinity.
proof_evidence: Convergence of discrete quadratic forms; exact secular equation x sin x+g sin(x theta)sin(x(1-theta))=0; zero-mode threshold g_c=-1/[theta(1-theta)] and negative-mode equation g=-kappa[coth(kappa theta)+coth(kappa(1-theta))]. Centered threshold g_c=-4 checked exactly.
costs: O(N) form evaluation; the saved exact checks use rational arithmetic only.
strongest_baseline: Bounded-potential eigenvalue comparison and rank-one interlacing against the clean path Laplacian.
falsifier: Failure of the discrete form to converge or a mismatching matching-condition/secular-equation derivation.
prior_art: Kunstatter and Louko, arXiv:1201.2886 (2012), https://arxiv.org/abs/1201.2886; not the same lattice defect model.
unresolved: Formal proof review of form convergence and compact-resolvent spectral convergence

claim: For free XX with any supplied Hermitian one-particle perturbation of rank at most r, scaled eigenvalues obey mu_(N,k+r)>=8J k^2. Exact Bernoulli factorization then gives a count-overflow archive bound log e_(N,D)<=-(4/3)tau J(D-1-r)^3+O((D-1-r)^2), uniformly in N and lambda on a compact interval. Bounded distributed W gives the same cubic leading exponent with changed lower-order constants.
quantifiers: Fixed rank r, fixed J,tau>0 and compact lambda interval; all N, D sufficiently larger than r. For W, assume uniformly bounded sampled potential and continuum convergence only for a limit-state claim.
proof_evidence: Rank-r eigenvalue interlacing, clean bound a_(N,k)>=8Jk^2, and the cycle-1 Chernoff count-tail proof; low-mode count is deterministically at most r.
costs: O(N) excitation-count encoding and log2(D) retained classical bits; decoder preparation cost uncharged.
strongest_baseline: Exact total-number sector code; stores the sufficient statistic M and reconstructs the lambda-independent conditional Gibbs state.
falsifier: A rank-r interlacing violation or a Bernoulli count-tail calculation contradicting the shifted cubic bound.
prior_art: Cycle-1 exact XX count-tail result, work/programmes/spin_statistical/leaves/leaf-01-local-critical-limit/RESULT.txt, sections 2, 5 and 6.

claim: For number-conserving H_(N,lambda)=H_(N,0)+U V_N-(lambda/L^2)M with U>=0, V_N>=0 and [V_N,M]=0, M remains an exact sufficient statistic. If the scaled one-body reference has a uniformly bounded finite set of low modes and a quadratic tail, sectorwise positivity plus min-max yields a cubic count-tail upper bound and hence a finite-dimensional archive.
quantifiers: Fixed U>=0, number-conserving positive interaction, compact lambda interval, and the explicitly stated uniform one-body spectral lower bound; no fixed deep scaled eigenvalue is allowed in this bound.
proof_evidence: Condition on M=m; the field factor is exp(tau lambda m). The interaction raises each m-sector Hamiltonian, so its sector partition trace is bounded by the corresponding free reference. Use Z_U>=1 and the free one-body product MGF. Exceptional bounded low modes add O(d^2) when Chernoff s=Theta(d^2).
costs: Archive label log2(D) bits; conditional-state decoder complexity uncharged.
strongest_baseline: Same number-sector code for the same known interacting Hamiltonian.
falsifier: A model satisfying the stated spectral and positivity bounds for which sector traces exceed the free reference or the tail fails.
prior_art: Cycle-1 sufficient-statistic construction for M, extended by the sector positivity comparison here.
unresolved: Fixed deep attractive defect with U>0 needs a separate denominator/sector-ground-state argument.

claim: The free XX whole-state Gibbs states converge in trace norm in the common Fock embedding for bounded distributed potentials, finite critical bulk point interactions, and finite-a Robin boundary tuning, provided the defect data are supplied. Fixed deep attractive boundary defects require a separate defect orbital; bare L2(0,1) embedding has no trace-norm limit for the occupied microscopic orbital. For interacting repulsive chains, whole-state convergence additionally requires fixed-particle-sector convergence and is not proved here.
quantifiers: Free case: fixed J,tau,compact lambda interval and fixed defect parameters under the listed critical scalings. Interacting case is a conditional statement only.
proof_evidence: Fixed eigenvalue/eigenfunction convergence from the limiting forms plus a uniform summable exp(-c k^2) occupation majorant; product Bernoulli trace distance is controlled by the l1 coordinate error. Deep localized mode concentrates on O(1) sites and must be factored into a separate slot.
costs: No numerical or oracle cost; identification of the known defect basis is part of the supplied decoder model.
strongest_baseline: Finite-sector exact Gibbs decomposition with a controlled particle-count tail.
falsifier: Failure of fixed-mode spectral convergence or of the summable occupation majorant under stated critical scaling.
prior_art: Kunstatter and Louko, arXiv:1201.2886 (2012), https://arxiv.org/abs/1201.2886, for the generic/tuned Robin distinction in another discretization.
unresolved: fixed-m sector convergence for fixed-U XXZ

claim: Boundedness and L^-2 saturation scaling alone do not imply whole-state convergence for an N-dependent site potential. If the uniform site coefficient is w_N/L^2 with w_N=0 for even N and w_N=c>0 for odd N, the two subsequences converge to distinct clean Fock Gibbs states at fields lambda and lambda-c, so the full sequence has no trace-norm limit.
quantifiers: Any fixed J,tau>0, c>0, and finite lambda; N alternates over even and odd integers.
proof_evidence: The perturbation is exactly (w_N/L^2)M, hence replaces lambda by lambda-w_N. The limiting first-mode occupation is strictly increasing in lambda, so the two subsequential states differ under a mode-occupation measurement.
strongest_baseline: A convergent-profile theorem, which includes a fixed W(x) and gives a single limiting continuum operator.
falsifier: Equality of the two distinct first-mode Bernoulli probabilities for c>0, which contradicts strict monotonicity.
unresolved: Only the need for profile convergence is claimed; homogenization for oscillatory profiles is not analyzed.
